Graph of the Influence of the Observations on an Equation

Source: R/plot_diagnostic.R
plot_influence.Rd

Selects the graph of a one-step measure of the influence of each observation on the coefficients of one equation: Cook's distance or the leverage. The five largest values are highlighted and labeled with the row number.

Usage

plot_influence(
  param,
  measure = "cook",
  adjust = TRUE,
  information = distributions7::expected_info(),
  legend = TRUE
)

Arguments

param

The equation, a parameter of the family.

measure

"cook" (the default) or "leverage".

adjust

Whether to divide the step by \(1 - h_i\).

information

An object from distributions7::expected_info() (the default) or distributions7::observed_info(), the matrix of the variance and of the weights \(w_i\).

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotInfluence object, inheriting from diagnostic_plot.

Details

Let \(X\) be the design of the equation param, \(s_i\) the contribution of observation \(i\) to the score of the equation on the scale of the link, \(w_i\) its information on that scale, and \(V\) the block of the Bayesian variance (bayesian_vcov()) of the coefficients of the equation, the inverse of the penalized information \(K\). Deleting the observation moves the coefficients, to first order, by $$\Delta_i = V x_i s_i,$$ with \(x_i\) the row of the design. The leverage is \(h_i = w_i x_i' V x_i\), the diagonal of the hat matrix, and its sum is the effective number of coefficients \(p_\text{eff}\) of the equation. Cook's distance is $$D_i = \Delta_i' K \Delta_i / p_\text{eff}.$$ With adjust = TRUE (the default) \(\Delta_i\) is divided by \(1 - h_i\), which is the Newton step from the full fit on the objective without the observation (the information \(K - w_i x_i x_i'\) by the Sherman-Morrison formula). For a gaussian mean with constant variance this step is the exact change of the least-squares coefficients, and \(D_i\) is the Cook distance of stats::cooks.distance() multiplied by \(\hat s^2/\hat\sigma^2\), the ratio of the residual variance of lm to the variance of the fit. With adjust = FALSE the step is \(V x_i s_i\) as stated. The coefficients of random effects and smooths are part of the equation, and the penalty is part of \(K\).

See also

plot_score(), diagnostics()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(100))
dd$y <- 1 + dd$x + rnorm(100, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_influence(param = "mu"))

ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_influence(param = "mu",
                                             measure = "leverage"))
